finding: The excerpt from Federalist No. 51 in the opening activity has a Flesch-Kincaid grade level of 12.4, well above the Grade 8 band. The sentence structure and vocabulary (e.g., 'usurpations,' 'encroachments') will impede independent comprehension for the target student population.
required_action: Replace the excerpt with a shorter, teacher-scaffolded version or provide a side-by-side plain-language glossary for all terms above a G8 reading level.

finding: In the Bill of Rights analysis station, the selected quote from the 1789 House debates is presented without any attribution to its source (Annals of Congress, vol. 1, p. 448). The text is also silently paraphrased in two places, which could mislead students about the original wording.
required_action: Add full source citation (Annals of Congress, date, page) and revert any paraphrased words to the exact original text using brackets for any editorial insertions.

finding: The 'Constitutional Convention Simulation' in Lesson 4 requires students to read two primary source position papers, hold a 15-minute committee debate, and draft a compromise proposal—realistically this sequence takes 60–70 minutes including transitions and role-assignment setup.
required_action: Split the activity into two 45-min periods (Day 1: reading + brief role prep; Day 2: debate + proposal), or cut one of the two position papers and shorten the debate to 10 minutes.

finding: Question 7 on the Module 31 exit ticket asks 'Which branch has the power to declare laws unconstitutional?' Both 'Judicial' and 'Supreme Court' are accepted as correct in the answer key, but the wording of the question and the provided choices makes both defensible, yet the key only marks one as correct.
required_action: Revise the prompt to specify 'which branch of government' or replace one of the two overlapping choices with a distractor such as 'Executive' or 'Legislative'.

finding: The bibliography for the primary source sets in Lesson 2 uses two different citation styles (Chicago footnote for one document, MLA parenthetical for another). This inconsistency could confuse students about expected citation conventions and does not align with the district’s prescribed style guide.
required_action: Standardize all citations in this module to the district’s preferred style (Chicago author-date), including the source list at the back of the teacher edition.

finding: Two of the four graphic organizers in the lesson are only provided as PDFs with no editable or text-based version, limiting screen-reader compatibility and preventing students from completing them digitally on school devices.
required_action: Provide each graphic organizer as a plain-text or Google Docs/Word version alongside the PDF, and ensure all text elements have proper alt-text descriptions.

finding: The module maps standard SS.C&G.8.3 (evaluate how the Constitution limits government power) to the 'Separation of Powers' lesson, but the activity focuses almost entirely on 'Checks and Balances' between branches, which is a different dimension of that standard per the North Carolina unpacking document.
required_action: Either re-align the lesson to the specific 'Separation of Powers' sub-standard by adding a direct comparison of the three branches’ independent powers, or change the mapped standard code to SS.C&G.8.4 (checks and balances).

finding: The 'Jigsaw: Article I–III' activity includes four reading passages plus a synthesis worksheet; with the average 8th-grade reading speed of ~150 wpm, students cannot finish the reading and complete the worksheet in 45 minutes unless the passages are shortened.
required_action: Trim each passage to 250 words maximum, or reduce the number of passages to three and combine the Executive and Judicial articles into a single handout.

finding: The teacher guide’s 'Background Notes' section for the Declaration of Independence activity includes a direct quote from John Locke’s Second Treatise but cites only 'Locke, 1690' without a precise page or section number. This makes the source unverifiable for students and teachers.
required_action: Add the specific section or page number (e.g., Second Treatise, §. 222, or the page from the Dover edition used in the curriculum), and include the edition in the works cited list.
